LintConfig.description:
The `[workspace.lint]` table: which rule groups run, per-rule severities, and per-directory overrides.

Precedence, lowest first: each rule's default, then this table, then every override whose `files` match, in file order — a later override wins over an earlier one, so list broad patterns before narrow ones. Within one table a rule's own setting beats a group toggle, and `disable` beats `enable`. A group toggle turns rules on or off but keeps the severity an earlier table chose.

A group toggle in an override replaces an explicit setting for a rule in `[workspace.lint]` (an override is more specific than the global table), but not one made by the same or an earlier override: overrides rank equal, so a rule's own setting there stands against any later group toggle. A later rule setting always wins. For example, with `CL001 = "off"` in `[workspace.lint]`, an override that enables `strict.calls` turns `CL001` on for its files; with `CL001 = "off"` in an override for `a/**`, a later override for `**/*.p` that enables `strict.calls` leaves `CL001` off.

An override with no `files` patterns, or only invalid ones, applies to no file and is reported as a warning.

The `default` group (the `LINT` rules) is always on: it cannot be toggled as a group, but each of its rules can be set to `off`. The `strict.*` groups are off until enabled.

disable.description: Rule groups to turn off. Applied after `enable` in the same table.

enable.description: Rule groups to turn on, for example `["strict.calls"]`. A dotted prefix selects every group under it: `"strict"` turns on every `strict.*` group.

overrides.description: Per-directory or per-file settings, applied in order after the global ones.

LintOverride.description: One `[[workspace.lint.overrides]]` entry: settings for the files that match `files`. An entry with no `files` applies to nothing.

disable.description: Rule groups to turn off. Applied after `enable` in the same table.

enable.description: Rule groups to turn on, for example `["strict.calls"]`. A dotted prefix selects every group under it: `"strict"` turns on every `strict.*` group.

files.description: Glob patterns relative to the directory holding `oxabl.toml`, written with `/` and matched case-insensitively. `*` stays inside one directory, `**` crosses directories, and a pattern that matches a directory selects every file under it.

LintSeverity.description: Severity of a lint rule; `off` disables it.

PreprocessorConfig.description:
The `[workspace.preprocessor]` table: the compile environment behind the AVM's predefined preprocessor names.

The AVM answers `{&OPSYS}`, `{&WINDOW-SYSTEM}`, `{&BATCH-MODE}`, `{&PROCESS-ARCHITECTURE}` and `{&PROVERSION}` from the machine it compiles on. A static analyzer has no such machine, so the environment is stated here and every `&IF` over one of these names is decided against it. The defaults describe a 64-bit Unix batch compile with a character (TTY) UI; set the keys to describe the environment your code is really compiled in.

`{&FILE-NAME}`, `{&LINE-NUMBER}` and `{&SEQUENCE}` are computed from the source and take no configuration.

The `DBTYPE`, `CONNECTED` and `LDBNAME` functions of an `&IF` ask which databases are connected, which only a compile knows. `databases` states them.

Container-level `#[serde(default)]` lets a partial table fall back per key, and `deny_unknown_fields` makes a misspelled key a hard error rather than a silently wrong branch.

batch-mode.description: Whether the compile is a batch compile; `{&BATCH-MODE}` expands to `yes` or `no`. Default `true`.

database-types.description: The `DBTYPE` of a connected database, by logical name, for example `{ ledger = "ORACLE" }`. A database that is not named here is `PROGRESS`.

databases.description:
The logical names of the databases connected when the code compiles. The `DBTYPE`, `CONNECTED` and `LDBNAME` functions of an `&IF` answer from this list, so `DBTYPE("ledger") NE ?` is true when `ledger` is listed.

When the key is absent, the `[workspace.schema]` files name the databases: the file name without `.df` is the logical name, so `schema/ledger.df` connects `ledger`. Set the key when a logical name differs from its file name, or to `[]` for a compile with no database connected. While neither a list nor a schema is given, an `&IF` that calls one of these functions raises `PREPROC010` instead of deciding on a guess.

proversion.description: Value of `{&PROVERSION}` and of the `PROVERSION` function, for example `"12.8"`. There is no default: the version is not something a tool can guess. While it is unset, an `&IF` condition that reads either form raises `PREPROC009` instead of silently deciding against an empty string.

directories.description: Directories to walk for ABL *root* files — `.p`, `.w`, `.cls`, and `.v`, matched case-insensitively. `.i` is deliberately not among them: an include fragment is never a root, and `is_root_file` is the one policy that decides.

include_paths.description: Include search paths, searched in order (PROPATH equivalent).

run_extensions.description:
Extensions tried, in order, for a `RUN` target written without one (`RUN post-order`), written without the dot. Default `["p", "w"]`.

A leading dot is ignored, and an entry that is empty or holds a path separator is dropped with a warning. Each extension is tried as written and then in lower case, against the name as written and then folded.

The first extension that finds a file wins. A list that omits an extension never links a bare name to such a file; an empty list links no bare name at all.

StyleGuide.description:
Comprehensive ABL style guide holding all formatting and diagnostic rules.

The struct uses `#[serde(default)]` so partial TOML files work: any missing field falls back to `Default::default()` which delegates to [`StyleGuide::default_base`]. It also uses `deny_unknown_fields` so a misspelled or unrecognized rule key is a hard error rather than being silently ignored — the config is user-facing, so a typo must fail loudly.

max_consecutive_blank_lines.description: Maximum number of consecutive blank lines the formatter permits before collapsing the run (and trimming file edges). This slice adds the field and its config plumbing only; enforcement lands with the Slice 3 printer.

lint.description: Lint rule groups, severities and per-directory overrides (`[workspace.lint]`).

preprocessor.description: The compile environment the preprocessor reports through its predefined names (`[workspace.preprocessor]`).

sources.description: Source file locations and include paths.

style.description:
Formatter style rules (`[workspace.style]`).

Embeds [`StyleGuide`] directly (no wrapper type): it already derives `Deserialize` with `#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]`, so a partial table fills unspecified fields from [`StyleGuide::default_base`], an absent section yields `default_base()`, and an unknown key is a hard parse error.
